intention: Wire inference_domain's `resolver` seam to the real local inference host, so the compile-once path actually reaches a model — and so `yield_report()` produces REAL numbers instead of measuring a stub.
why: MEASURED 2026-07-26. inference_domain sits on the build order as DONE and the librarian is planned on top of it. Its own filed edge (b) says: 'THE HOST CLIENT is injected (the `resolver` seam) and not yet wired to a real host — it will live HERE and nowhere else.' The record was honest at the component and wrong at the plan. Worse: a working host has been running on this box the entire time and nothing in Cairn knew — `ollama serve` (pid 2136) up since 2026-07-22, listening on :11434, with qwen2.5:7b, llama3.2:1b and nomic-embed-text. Both endpoints measured working on 2026-07-26 (embeddings returned 768 dimensions; generation responded). Nothing in the tree references port 11434, ollama, or that endpoint. THE SECOND WHY IS THE BIGGER ONE: `yield_report()` measures tokens SPENT on misses against tokens AVOIDED by hits. That is the instrument for telos aim 1 — the measured curve of resolver-calls declining as the corpus grows. Akien's most showcaseable claim (a prebuild step saving ~90% of tokens, independently reimplemented at his workplace and running daily) has no recorded measurement inside Cairn. This node is what turns that instrument on.
traces_to: telos aim 1 — demonstrate inference compilation. Unmeasurable until the meter reads a real host.
Law 3 — nothing is known until measured. The cache's yield is currently a hypothesis measured against a stub.
Law 6 — the host client lives in inference_domain and nowhere else; this node fills that seam and adds no second path.
Law 8 — the sole-path tooth (a tester import-scan that reds any other module opening the host) is inference_domain's own filed edge (b), and this node is what makes that tooth worth growing.
state: code-seam@v1: THINKME -> BUILDME -> PROVEME -> LEARNME -> PROVED   (CAST 2026-07-26 via /sorted; cursor at BUILDME. Leaf. Gate ran, not red — two distinctions recorded.)

gates.prove_gate: proof gate — the tester runs the proof and emits a VALIDATION.

falsifier: Against the REAL host: (1) a first request resolves and returns an answer; (2) an IDENTICAL second request is a HIT and the resolver is NEVER called — asserted by instrumenting the resolver, not inferred from timing; (3) `yield_report()` shows tokens AVOIDED strictly greater than zero, and the avoided/spent numbers reconcile against the two calls. That is the compile-once claim proved end to end rather than asserted. A hollow build fails (2) — returning a cached-looking answer while still calling the host is exactly the failure this must catch. Additionally the host's ABSENCE must be a declared, loud failure, not a crash: the box can be rebooted, the service can be down, and 'inference host unreachable' is a legitimate measured state (Law 7).
horizon: The yield number is meaningless until real traffic runs through it. Re-read once the librarian or the reading work has driven a few hundred requests — before then the curve has too few points to say anything, and quoting it early would be the same error as quoting an unmeasured 90%.
distinctions_recorded: THE HOST IS NOT HEX. `hex` does not resolve, is not in /etc/hosts, and is not on the ARP table — the M1 remains a plan. What exists is ollama on THIS box. That is fine and it is the point of the seam: build and prove against localhost now, and Hex later becomes a HOST SWAP behind the same seam. The librarian therefore does NOT wait on acquiring or wiring an M1, which is a materially different dependency picture from the one held-librarian assumed.

EMBEDDINGS ARE A DIFFERENT CALL SHAPE AND ARE NOT IN SCOPE HERE. inference_domain does completion-shaped caching; nomic-embed-text is an embedding endpoint. Both live on the same host, but wiring the completion resolver does not give the system embeddings, and pretending otherwise would repeat the done-but-not-connected defect this node exists to close. Whether Cairn wants a pretrained embedder AT ALL is Akien's open call — his objection stands ('every call is an inference call', so the curve never bends), with the word graph as the real answer and an off-the-shelf embedder at most a bootstrap that must carry a written exit condition.
